text:
maya: quick heads up — after yesterday's kernel tiling change I see KV prefix cache hit-rate drop on chat workloads :eyes:
perf-bot: alert triggered: cache_hit_rate < 70% for model=longchat-70b in region=us-west (last 60m)
aj: ugh, that's the attn_tiling_v2 rollout. what numbers are we seeing?
maya: baseline pre-change was ~88% overall for convo-prefix keys. post-change it's ~61% and P95 latency increased ~18ms for tail requests. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/rr/cache?model=longchat-70b
samir: do we know whether keys actually changed or eviction just increased? can you run a quick op-level profile?
maya: ran a short trace: `redwood profile --model longchat-70b --trace cache-ops --last 30m` output snippet:
```
cache_ops: total=124k
  lookup_hits=75k (60.5%)
  lookup_misses=49k (39.5%)
  evictions=8.2k
  avg_lookup_ns=4200
  avg_store_ns=5200
  keys_normalized=false
```
maya: interestingly keys_normalized=false — we still used raw byte prefixes for keys, and the tile change zero-pads internal buffers which seems to flip the bytes for stray boundary tokens
nina: that would explain it — kernel tiling changed buffer alignment, producing different bytes for the same logical token sequence. we need canonicalization by tokenizer normalization or token id sequence as key.
aj: agree. we should also check whether batching heuristics changed request ordering causing miss amplification (different prefix lengths seen by the cache).
samir: two quick ideas: 1) normalize keys to token ids (sha1 of token ids + model + role), 2) prefetch/pin common convo prefixes on session start for hot orgs.
maya: ran a quick sim: replaced raw bytes with canonical token-id key and re-ran against last 1h logs (local sim) — hit-rate jumped from 61% -> 87% on the simulated replay. sim command:
```
# offline replay
redwood replay --input logs/2025-11-09/longchat-ops.json --key-fn "tokenid_sha1(model, role, tokens[:prefix_len])" --metrics cache_hit_rate
```
oliver: nice. what's the perf cost of doing tokenization normalization on the hot path? we've avoided running tokenizer on the runtime for perf reasons.
maya: tokenization cost is small compared to the benefit if we do it only for cache key generation and we can cache the mapping per-request in-process. measured ~0.4ms extra per new convo start, amortized down with prefetch.
aj: another angle — batching heuristics: we saw the new kernel reordered batches for throughput, causing more variable prefix lengths and cold misses. if we stripe prefetch across shards we can warm multiple cache nodes in parallel.
nina: propose a short rollback for attn_tiling_v2 for the rollout on production while we deploy key normalization + a warmup job. we can land a targeted patch that canonicalizes keys before store/lookup.
maya: agreed. also adding a background warmup worker that, on session create, issues a lightweight `prefetch_prefix` RPC to the model shard to populate KV for common prefixes. cheap: `prefetch_prefix(prefix_id)` returns `true` when present.
samir: please add an exp flag to enable prefetching per-org; we should A/B it on a few customers.
aj: note: need to update observability to break down cache hit-rate by workload type (chat vs completion vs RAG) — current metric is aggregate and hides that RAG workloads remain ~92% but chat tanked.
maya: filed a quick ticket: https://go/redwood/issue/INF-3145 — will push canonicalization PR and warmup worker today, plan to rollback attn_tiling_v2 in the meantime.
perf-bot: deploy rollback scheduled: attn_tiling_v2 -> attn_tiling_v1 at 2025-11-10T03:15:00Z by infra-ops.
oliver: after canonicalization landed, add a unit test that ensures key invariance across kernel tiling variants (simulate zero-padding). also add a microbenchmark for token-id conversion cost.
nina: thumbs-up. thanks team — target: stabilize hit-rate >85% before end of day and re-evaluate batching heuristics next week. :thumbsup:
maya: will post follow-up with before/after numbers once PR is live.
